summary_paragraph: A woman with end-stage renal disease, diabetes, morbid obesity, and a history of recurrent abscesses and thromboses was admitted for a right groin abscess that had drained spontaneously. She was febrile on presentation and received incision and drainage in the ED, followed by IV vancomycin. Blood cultures remained negative, and she remained afebrile throughout the hospitalization. A CT scan showed no deep pelvic infection, and a right lower extremity ultrasound ruled out DVT despite initial concern on imaging. The abscess improved with packing and antibiotics. Her INR remained therapeutic on warfarin, and she continued her home medications for heart failure, pulmonary hypertension, and diabetes. She completed a dialysis session on the day of discharge and was transitioned to oral sevelamer and Nephrocaps. She was discharged to extended care with wound care instructions, a seven-day course of vancomycin via dialysis, and guidance to monitor weight and symptoms.
